strategy_definition.summary: A systematic framework to identify and anticipate Seek and Destroy consolidation conditions after price sweeps both sides of market liquidity, reverts to 50% equilibrium, and PD arrays fail to follow through.

timeframes.notes: Demonstrated using Daily and 4-hour charts to spot macro consolidation, PD array failures, and eventual displacement.

other: Both sell-side and buy-side liquidity pools swept in a single major expansion leg

glossary.SEEK AND DESTROY: Market conditions characterized by price seeking liquidity on both sides, sweeping highs and lows to trap both long and short traders.
glossary.PD ARRAYS NOT FOLLOWING THROUGH: When premium or discount arrays (such as FVGs and Order Blocks) fail to produce expected price rejections and expansions, leading to wick-heavy candles.

custom_signals.name: equilibrium_reversion
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price gravitating back to the 50% equilibrium midpoint of the recent range formed by the dual liquidity sweep.

custom_signals.name: pd_array_failure
custom_signals.plain_definition: Premium or discount arrays fail to hold or push price in their intended direction, resulting in wick-filled candles with no follow-through FVGs.

custom_signals.name: htf_range_displacement
custom_signals.plain_definition: A higher-timeframe expansion creating an FVG cleanly outside the consolidation boundary, confirming an exit from Seek and Destroy conditions.

sequence: Identify major sell-side liquidity swept at the low of an existing consolidation [01:08].
Observe price aggressively expand in one leg to sweep opposing buy-side liquidity at the range highs [01:28].
Apply Fibonacci across that expansion range from low to high to locate the 50% equilibrium level [01:51].
Observe price pull back toward equilibrium, where price enters balance and generates new liquidity [01:59].
Monitor subsequent interactions with PD arrays; confirm Seek and Destroy conditions once premium and discount arrays fail to reject or follow through [02:19, 03:21].
Avoid directional trend trading within the range until a higher timeframe creates displacement (FVG) breaking cleanly out of the consolidation [05:45].

invalidation.text: Seek and Destroy conditions terminate when price displaces cleanly out of the consolidation range on a higher timeframe leaving an FVG, and PD arrays resume following through.

filters.text: Trend-following traders must stop trading or stay out of the market once PD arrays fail to follow through near equilibrium.
Do not consider lower-timeframe (e.g. 1-minute) fair value gaps as valid displacement out of the consolidation range; displacement must be on a higher timeframe.

entry_rule.text: No execution entry taught in this video; the presenter identifies market conditions here and states actionable capitalization rules (turtle soups) will be covered in episode 28.
entry_rule.quote: in the next episode I exactly want to go over Turtle soups and I want to go over how we can potentially capitalize on these conditions

target_rule.text: Price refers back like a magnet to the 50% equilibrium level of the expansion range after sweeping both sides.
target_rule.quote: like a Magnus price will refer back to the 50 percent of that most recent range which is that that is equilibrium

presenter_claims.claim: Consolidation at the 50% equilibrium is guaranteed once PD arrays stop following through.
Displacement out of Seek and Destroy conditions usually happens during NFP, CPI, or FOMC news releases.

strategy_definition.notes: This video defines an environmental regime identification and filtering methodology rather than a mechanical entry trigger. It provides objective criteria to classify price action as non-trending consolidation, alerting traders to either stand aside or adapt to turtle soup setups.

confidence.reason: The sequence of events (dual sweeps, 50% equilibrium reversion, PD array failure, and HTF displacement exit) is clearly articulated and demonstrated.

Price immediately targets and sweeps the opposing buy-side liquidity at the highs.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price takes out a major liquidity pool and refers back to 50% equilibrium.
Price enters an FVG and an order block but fails to follow through, leaving wick-heavy price action.
A new higher-timeframe FVG forms that completely displaces out of the gray consolidation range, confirming the end of Seek and Destroy conditions.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: He shows how to recognize the end of the consolidation. A lower-timeframe FVG is not enough; you need a higher-timeframe displacement (usually news-driven like NFP/CPI) completely clearing the consolidation area.

may_differ.reason: Traidle would detect the structural FVG, but requires a custom module to evaluate its position strictly relative to a drawn consolidation box.
